title: File system API on PostgreSQL
idea: As a Node.js service, the file tree becomes one `fs_node` table with parent links, behind an Express API; constraints settle races and a recursive query sums sizes.
points: Each row stores `parent_id`, name, kind and size; the root has no parent.
`UNIQUE (parent_id, name)` makes duplicate names impossible, even for racing requests.
A recursive CTE sums a whole subtree in one query, like `du`.
Follow-up: a stored full-path column makes lookups one query but makes moves costly.

hero.title: A duplicate create loses at the database

steps.caption: Two identical requests to create `/docs/plan.txt` leave the client at once. Follow one.
The controller parses the body with zod: an absolute path, a kind, a size.
The service resolves `/docs` one name at a time and checks it is a folder.
The repository sends one INSERT. No check-then-insert in code, so no gap to race in.
The twin request inserted first. The unique constraint refuses this row with code `23505`.
The service maps `23505` to a domain error: ALREADY_EXISTS with status 409.
Error middleware turns it into a JSON body. The client sees 409; its twin saw 201.

code.title: Express + PostgreSQL
code.caption: Repository, service, controllers and error mapping in one file, run against a real PostgreSQL with happy paths, a race and failures.

walk.text: BIGINT reads as a JS number, safe below 2^53. CHECKs refuse empty or slashed names; deletes cascade.
The recursive CTE starts at one node and keeps joining children.
Resolve walks the path one query per name, failing with 404 or 409.
Create lets the database decide: 23505 means taken, 23503 means the parent vanished.
Zod accepts only absolute paths without dot segments; create also refuses the root.
Express 5 sends async errors here; map validation, domain and unknown errors to status codes.
Build a tree, try three bad paths, race a duplicate, then list, size and delete.

pitfalls: Do not check for a name, then insert; let the unique constraint decide.
Plain `UNIQUE` lets NULL parents repeat; `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` blocks duplicate top-level names only.
Follow-up: moving a folder is one `UPDATE` of `parent_id`, after a cycle check.

quiz.q: What does the `race statuses` line print?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: Both requests reach the INSERT. The unique constraint lets exactly one row in; the other gets 23505, which the service maps to 409. Sorting fixes the order.

takeaway: Let constraints settle races; let a recursive query walk the tree.

starters: Interview follow-up: how would I store file contents, not only sizes?
Interview follow-up: how do I move a folder with one UPDATE and stay cycle-free?
Interview follow-up: would a materialized path column make lookups faster?
